cp-1.title: Beginner cherry keyring
cp-1.caption: Yarn: 4-ply cotton, 3.0mm hook. Watch the ring — it can be done in a day!
cp-1.review: I worked the ring stitches tight in single crochet. Made three more as gifts.

cp-2.title: Pastel rainbow scarf
cp-2.caption: Yarn: 100% merino, 4.5mm needles. Took about two weeks!
cp-2.review: Color changes were a little fussy for stitch count, but finishing felt great. Knit extra length after wrapping it around your neck.

cp-3.title: Teddy body chart
cp-3.caption: After stuffing, I joined the body and head with a stitch bind.
cp-3.review: Eye buttons are sewn on. Stuff lightly so the silhouette stays cute. Perfect as a kid gift!

cp-4.title: Basic winter beanie
cp-4.caption: Yarn: gray acrylic, 5.0mm circulars. A 20×20 all-knit basic.
cp-4.review: All knit in the round, beginner-friendly. Circular needles mean no seam.

cp-5.title: Mini heart coaster
cp-5.caption: I made a set of four and shared them with friends.
cp-5.review: Looks adorable on the table. Follow the heart chart and it won’t fail.

cp-6.title: Done! Beige cardigan
cp-6.caption: Yarn: 100% merino, 4.5mm needles. Took about two weeks!
cp-6.review: Sleeve decreases were confusing until Tteuni helped. Keep the body easy; add 14 rows on the sleeves for a better length.

cp-7.title: Cozy white gloves
cp-7.caption: Yarn: white merino, 3.5mm DPNs. Simple stockinette on the back of the hand.
cp-7.review: Go slow on the finger split and beginners can follow. 2×2 rib at the wrist keeps them snug.

cp-8.title: Pink star coaster
cp-8.caption: Yarn: 3-ply pink cotton, 4.0mm hook. About one dinner’s worth of knitting.
cp-8.review: Pinch star points in single crochet for a crisp shape. Pair with the heart coaster on the table.

cp-9.title: Cozy pink socks
cp-9.caption: Yarn: pink sock wool, 2.5mm DPNs. Heel turned with short rows.
cp-9.review: Match instep gauge and length is easy to tweak. Write down stitch counts after the first sock so the pair matches.

cp-10.title: Yellow beanie
cp-10.caption: Yarn: bulky yellow acrylic, 5.5mm circulars. Same basic as the gray beanie.
cp-10.review: I only changed the color from the gray basic. About 8 brim rib rows roll nicely. Take the crown decreases slowly.

qa-1.title: How do I keep stitch count on a magic ring?
qa-1.excerpt: Following the beginner cherry keyring, the ring always opens into a hole…
qa-1.body:
Hi! Every time I work the ring on round 3 of the cherry keyring, a hole opens up.

I’m using 4-ply yarn and a 3.5mm hook. The chart says 6 single crochet, but mine always feels more like 8.

Am I holding the stitches too loosely? Tips from anyone who’s been there!

qa-2.title: How to lengthen beige cardigan sleeves
qa-2.excerpt: It’s the cardigan from the showcase — I want the sleeves about 5cm longer.
qa-2.body:
I’m knitting the beige cardigan from the showcase, and the arms feel short.

If I keep the body as-is, how many extra sleeve rows do I need? Gauge is about 22 sts / 28 rows in 10cm.

qa-3.title: When yarn color doesn’t match the chart
qa-3.excerpt: I bought coral yarn and it’s much redder than on screen. Looking for a swap.
qa-3.body:
The community preview looks like a soft coral, but in real life it’s closer to #FC5F53 and too loud.

Any similar-tone substitutes, or a way to tone the color down?

qa-4.title: Grid won’t load in the pattern editor
qa-4.excerpt: I tapped import from a community card and only got an empty grid.
qa-4.body:
Tried in Chrome, and I’m logged in. Only one chart (cp-3) does this, even after refresh.

Could it be local storage space?

qa-5.title: Seam line when knitting a beanie in the round
qa-5.excerpt: 20×20 gray all-knit basic — even on circulars the start of the round tilts.
qa-5.body:
I’m knitting the basic winter beanie in the round on 5.0mm circulars.

It’s all knit, but the start of each round slowly slants like a seam. Should I move the marker, or jog the start by one stitch?

qa-6.title: Confused about splitting glove fingers
qa-6.excerpt: The back of the hand is fine — I don’t know when to split the thumb and fingers.
qa-6.body:
Following the cozy white gloves. Wrist rib is 2 knit / 2 purl, then stockinette on the hand.

How do I divide leftover stitches for the fingers? Where should stitch markers go? Using 3.5mm DPNs.

qa-7.title: A hole appeared while turning a pink sock heel
qa-7.excerpt: One sock is done but the heel corner is gappy. I want to fix it before sock two.
qa-7.body:
I finished the first cozy pink sock. Instep gauge is fine, but short-row heel turns left a hole.

I saw the note about writing stitch counts — how do I close the hole? Should I pick up extra stitches?

qa-8.title: Can heart and star coasters share the same stitch count?
qa-8.excerpt: I want them as a table set and worry they’ll end up different sizes.
qa-8.body:
The mini heart coaster is 12×12, and the pink star coaster is 12×12 too.

Same 3-ply cotton and 4.0mm hook — will they match in real size? If I pinch the star points in single crochet, will they look like a set with the heart?

qa-9.title: The rainbow scarf has no chart — how do I follow it?
qa-9.excerpt: There’s only a photo, no grid. Is the stripe order enough?
qa-9.body:
The pastel rainbow scarf post says no attached chart. I only see the AI preview.

Do I just repeat the stripe colors? Can I knit it flat on 4.5mm circulars, or should it be in the round?

qa-10.title: Are the yellow beanie and gray hat really the same chart?
qa-10.excerpt: I want to swap only the color and need to confirm stitch and row counts.
qa-10.body:
The yellow beanie notes say it’s the same chart as the gray basic.

Are both 20×20? Yellow looks like 5.5mm circulars and gray 5.0mm — will the shape still match with different needles? How many brim rib rows work well?

answers.ans-1: Twist the hook a little as you work the ring and the hole shrinks. Keep round 1 tight, then don’t let round 2 loosen.
answers.ans-2: Mark stitch counts with scrap yarn so growth shows immediately. If the target is 6, knit 5 and check before the last one.
answers.ans-3: At that gauge, 5cm is about 14 extra rows. Finish the last two sleeve rows with a snugger stitch.
answers.ans-4: Measure the showcase beige cardigan photo against your wrist — that makes the extra-row math easier.
answers.ans-5: Cotton coral reads louder than on screen. Blend a beige row, or go up a needle size for a softer look.
answers.ans-6: The teddy chart does import. If you get an empty grid, tap Import to editor again from the community card.
answers.ans-7: In-the-round stockinette jogs one stitch each round. Park a marker at the start, and if it leans, change rounds one stitch earlier.
answers.ans-8: Split the hand stitches into four, then pick the thumb from the side. Hang scrap markers in four spots before the split.
answers.ans-9: Pick up the neighboring stitch at the turning corner to close the hole. Keep sock one’s counts beside you for sock two.
answers.ans-10: Same yarn and hook size, they’ll nearly match. Shorten the star points a little and they sit well with the heart.
answers.ans-11: There’s no chart — use the stripe order. Flat on circulars is fine; in the round has no seam.
answers.ans-12: Both grids are 20×20 all knit. 0.5mm thicker needles make it a bit bigger, so aim for about 8 brim rib rows.

comments.fc-1: The color is gorgeous! If you’re lengthening sleeves, about 14 extra rows should do it.
comments.fc-2: I followed the chart as written and the size was perfect. Thank you!
comments.fc-3: When you add the teddy ears, use only a little stuffing. Too much and they look mashed.
comments.fc-4: I added a bit of wrist rib and the gloves stay on. Finger splits are easier with scrap markers.
comments.fc-5: I made these with the heart coaster. Pinching star points in single crochet keeps the shape.
comments.fc-6: Heel turning was new so I fussed, but writing counts after sock one made sock two match.
comments.fc-7: Same chart as the gray basic so it was quick. Yellow looks great for spring.
